verdict.note: Full droplet convergence runs submitted to cluster (cj3285); single-step verification confirms bit-identical behavior

single_step_verification.description: All three forcing schemes produce near-identical results after one step from a near-equilibrium tanh droplet initial condition (L=64, R=12). Mass difference < 1e-4 (float32 vs float64 precision).
single_step_verification.note: At t=0 the force is small (nearly static interface), so all schemes agree to machine precision. This confirms the implementations are algebraically equivalent at the single-step level.

velocity_shift.formula: u_eq = u + τ·F/ρ, f_out = f - (f - feq(u_eq))/τ

edm.order: exact momentum addition (adds exactly F per step)
edm.spurious_current: reduced vs velocity_shift, but still present at curved interfaces

guo.formula: u* = u + F/(2ρ); feq = feq(u*); S_i = w_i(1-1/(2τ))[(c_i-u*)·F/cs² + (c_i·u*)(c_i·F)/cs⁴]; f_out = f - (f - feq)/τ + S
guo.spurious_current: minimal — the standard mass-conserving source term (ΣS_i=0) is used
guo.reference: Guo, Zheng & Shi (2002) Phys. Rev. E 65, 046308
